newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks surge for 7th day, hit new record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks surge for 7th day, hit new record.

text.p: Caracas stocks surged in strong trade for the seventh consecutive session to a record high on positive growth prospects for the coming year, traders said.
"The trend is definitely up. The market has a positive outlook for 1997 and a number of investors taking positions on that," said Financorp broker Hector Perez.
Ministers have said economic growth will reach four percent in 1997, reversing 1996's 1.6 percent fall.
The market's leading index gained 2.02 percent to close at 6,607.23 points as 33 shares rose, 10 fell and five closed flat, according to preliminary figures from the bourse.

A total of 51.6 million shares traded, worth 12.43 billion bolivars ($26 million). Volume was boosted by trade of nearly 19 million shares in Corimon Type B stock, which closed off 0. 25 bolivars at 8.75 bolivars.

Leading bank Banco Provincial's share price also adjusted to 895 bolivars on a share dividend for each 3.57 shares held on December 26. The stock ended up at 900.00 bolivars after closing Thursday at 1145.00.
